summary: GRN 1256 is a resubmission by Plantible Foods for Lemna Leaf Protein (LLP), a highly purified (≥80% protein) extract from Lemna minor, intended for use as a protein ingredient in 11 food categories. The notice is substantively complete: identity, specifications, five-batch data, manufacturing process, dietary exposure, and allergenicity are all documented. The pivotal toxicological anchor is the published Kawamata et al. (2020) 90-day rat study conducted with Wolffia globosa Mankai powder; the notice explicitly acknowledges FDA's conclusion that the NOAEL is the mid-dose (6.5 g/kg bw/day) and provides a margin-of-exposure analysis. The test-article bridge from Mankai and LPC to LLP is structured and compositionally supported, though the cross-species, cross-processing gap is the central evidentiary tension. An unpublished 90-day LENTEIN Complete gavage study is correctly characterized as supportive. The expert panel statement relies substantially on GRN 742 comparator framing. Literature search methodology is documented and updated through January 2025. The most material residual issues are: (1) the adequacy of the margin of exposure when FDA's preferred NOAEL (6.5 g/kg bw/day) is used with the highest-intake age group (ages 4-8, 0.719 g/kg bw/day, MOS=9); (2) the cross-species, cross-processing bridge from Mankai/LPC to LLP; and (3) the expert panel's framing of the evaluation as substantially equivalent to GRN 742 rather than as a fully independent analysis. No critical evidentiary gaps are identified; the most significant issues are adequacy gaps in the bridge and margin-of-exposure arguments.

findings.title: Margin of exposure below 10 for ages 4-8 when FDA-preferred NOAEL is applied
findings.summary: FDA concluded in its review letter that the NOAEL from Kawamata et al. (2020) is the mid-dose (6.5 g/kg bw/day for males), not the highest dose. The notice acknowledges this and calculates MOS values of 23 (ages 2+) and 9 (ages 4-8) using the mid-dose NOAEL. A MOS of 9 for the highest-consuming pediatric age group (ages 4-8, 90th percentile 0.719 g/kg bw/day) is below the conventional 10-fold safety factor threshold. The notice argues that the EDI is extremely conservative (100% market penetration at maximum use levels), that protein is a macronutrient with well-understood metabolism, and that it is not feasible to achieve a 100-fold margin with a macronutrient ingredient without creating nutritional imbalance. These arguments are substantive but the adequacy of the margin for the pediatric subgroup remains the central unresolved quantitative safety question.
findings.recommendedAction: Provide a more detailed probabilistic or tiered exposure analysis for ages 4-8 that moves beyond the 100% market penetration assumption, and explicitly address whether the dose-dependent findings in the Kawamata study (fibrinogen, cholesterol, phospholipids, electrolytes) have any biological relevance at the estimated pediatric exposure levels. Consider whether a use restriction for foods primarily consumed by young children is warranted.

MOS calculation: 6.5/0.719 = 9

findings.title: Cross-species, cross-processing bridge from Mankai and LPC to LLP requires stronger compositional anchoring for pivotal toxicology study
findings.summary: The pivotal 90-day toxicology study (Kawamata et al. 2020) used dried Wolffia globosa Mankai powder (~43-46% protein dw), a different genus and a less-processed product than LLP (≥80% protein, Lemna minor, extensively purified by maceration, decantation, chlorophyll flocculation, activated carbon adsorption, microfiltration, and ultrafiltration). The notice provides a structured compositional bridge covering amino acid profiles, anti-nutrients, heavy metals, and macronutrients, and argues that compositional differences (higher protein concentration, lower fiber, lower manganese, higher copper, lower carotenoids/Vitamin K) do not adversely affect the bridge. The copper difference (LLP <41 ppm vs Mankai <8.6 ppm) is addressed quantitatively. The bridge is scientifically reasoned but rests on the assumption that the purification process does not introduce or concentrate novel bioactive components beyond those characterized. The proteomics analysis (14 proteins, >90% of mass) strengthens the bridge for protein identity. The bridge is partial rather than missing because the compositional comparison is systematic and the differences are addressed, but the cross-genus, cross-processing gap is acknowledged by EFSA and FDA.
findings.recommendedAction: Strengthen the bridge by explicitly addressing whether the ultrafiltration and activated carbon steps could concentrate or generate any novel peptides or process-related impurities not present in Mankai, and confirm that the proteomics characterization of LLP is representative of commercial-scale production batches rather than a single laboratory preparation.

findings.title: Expert panel frames evaluation primarily as substantial equivalence to GRN 742 rather than independent analysis
findings.summary: The expert panel consensus statement (Appendix 7) explicitly states that 'The evaluation of LLP is largely based on its substantial equivalence to LENTEIN Complete, described in GRN 742' and that 'FDA issued a No Objections letter to GRN 742 on August 22, 2018.' While the panel does conduct its own review of the compositional data, toxicology studies, and allergenicity assessment, the framing relies on GRN 742's outcome as a reference anchor. The notice does identify the underlying information from GRN 742 and explains its role, and the panel states its own conclusion. However, the repeated invocation of GRN 742's 'No Objections' letter as a basis for confidence, rather than as context, risks substituting a prior regulatory outcome for an independent scientific conclusion. The main dossier is more analytically independent than the expert panel statement.
findings.recommendedAction: Revise the expert panel statement to clearly distinguish between (a) information drawn from GRN 742 that is independently evaluated and found applicable, and (b) the panel's own independent conclusion based on the totality of evidence. Remove or reframe language that implies the GRN 742 'No Objections' letter itself is a basis for the GRAS conclusion for LLP.

findings.title: Unpublished 90-day LENTEIN Complete gavage study correctly characterized as supportive but its role in the weight of evidence should be explicit
findings.summary: The notice references an unpublished 90-day repeat-dose oral toxicity study with LENTEIN Complete in Wistar rats (OECD 408, gavage, up to 1000 mg/kg bw/day) reported by Parabel in GRN 742. The notice correctly states 'As this information is not published in a peer review journal, it provides supportive but not pivotal information to this safety assessment.' The pivotal toxicology evidence (Kawamata et al. 2020) is public and peer-reviewed. The characterization is appropriate and the calibration rule is satisfied: the unpublished study is supportive, not pivotal, and does not downgrade the public-pivotal-evidence assessment. This is a minor documentation note rather than a gap.
findings.recommendedAction: No corrective action required. The notice correctly characterizes the unpublished study as supportive. Consider adding a brief statement in the weight-of-evidence summary explicitly noting that the GRAS conclusion does not depend on the unpublished study.

findings.title: Copper specification for LLP (up to 41 ppm) is substantially higher than Mankai and warrants explicit dietary margin confirmation
findings.summary: LLP has a copper specification of <41 ppm (mean 38 ppm across three batches), compared to Mankai's specification of <8.6 ppm. The notice addresses this in Section 6.3.3 by calculating that at 20% dietary inclusion in rodents, LLP would contribute at most 8 ppm copper, within the range of standard rodent diets (13 ppm in Lab Diet 5002). The notice also provides a human dietary intake analysis in Table 34 showing that 90th percentile copper intake from LLP (0.37-0.81 mg/day depending on age group) combined with background intakes remains below the IOM Tolerable Upper Intake Level for all age groups. The analysis is present and quantitative. The residual question is whether the conservative assumption of 100% market penetration at maximum inclusion adequately bounds the upper tail of copper exposure for ages 1-3, for whom background intake data are not available from WWEIA.
findings.recommendedAction: Confirm that the copper intake estimate for ages 1-3 is bounded by available background intake data or provide a sensitivity analysis using the most conservative plausible background intake for this age group to demonstrate that combined copper intake remains below the UL of 1 mg/day.

evidenceMatrix.assessment: The notice provides a structured bridge covering amino acid profiles (Tables 6-9), macronutrient composition (Tables 5, 12, 17), mineral content (Table 14), anti-nutrients and contaminants (Table 18), and proteomics identity (Table 11). The bridge is documented but its adequacy is contested by regulatory authorities.

safetySignals.label: Margin of exposure below 10 for ages 4-8 at FDA-preferred NOAEL
safetySignals.summary: Using FDA's preferred NOAEL of 6.5 g/kg bw/day (mid-dose from Kawamata et al. 2020), the margin of exposure for the highest-consuming pediatric subgroup (ages 4-8, 90th percentile 0.719 g/kg bw/day) is approximately 9, below the conventional 10-fold safety factor. The notice provides arguments for why the EDI is conservative and why protein macroingredients do not require a 100-fold margin, but the adequacy of this margin for children is the central unresolved quantitative safety question in this resubmission.

safetySignals.label: EFSA manganese concern for related duckweed products distinguished but not fully resolved for LLP
safetySignals.summary: EFSA declined to establish safety for LENTEIN Complete, Mankai powder, and whole L. minor/L. gibba plant material primarily due to manganese levels (59.6-333 ppm in those products). LLP has a manganese specification of <12 ppm (actual values 9.6-12 ppm), substantially lower than the products that raised EFSA concern. The notice attributes this to the ultrafiltration process and provides a quantitative dietary intake analysis for manganese (Table 33) showing intakes below the UL. EFSA approved the ABC Kroos BV water lentil protein concentrate (L. minor/L. gibba, manganese <100 ppm) in 2023. The manganese concern is effectively distinguished for LLP based on documented low levels, and this signal is clear rather than a gap.
